newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues Telecom sees 1 bln FFr '97 sales.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues Telecom sees 1 bln FFr '97 sales.

text.p: Bouygues Telecom, a subsidiary of the construction conglomerate, should have a 1997 sales figure of about one billion francs against 160 million in 1996, said managing director Patrick Leleu.
Bouygues Telecom started France's third mobile telecommunications network six months ago and has the ambition to become a national operator from 1998 when the French sectior is liberalised.
Leleu told a news conference the company expected to have 300,000 subscribers by the end of 1997.
It had 60,700 at the end of October and expects to add 90,000 to that before the end of the year.
"Our aim remains to take a 20 percent market share at end 2000 when the market is estimated to count between seven and eight million users," he said.

In 1999, the Bouygues Telecom network should cover 90 percent of the French population, against some 20 percent now. To achieve this, investments will be some two billion francs in 1996 and three billion in 1997 after one billion in 1995.
